# Credential Management

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Overview

Windmill provides built-in credential management where secrets are encrypted
at rest in PostgreSQL using a workspace-specific symmetric key [6][7]. This
is the #2 requirement: the PA (an LLM) must never hold credentials; the
engine manages secrets and the PA triggers workflows by ID/webhook without
accessing auth.

## Encryption Model

| Aspect | Details | Source |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Key type | Symmetric, workspace-specific | [7] |
| Key length | 64 alphanumeric characters | [7] |
| Key generation | Automatic at workspace creation | [7] |
| Key storage | workspace_settings table in PostgreSQL | [7] |
| Algorithm | Not specified in documentation | [7] |
| Key rotation | Supported, automatic re-encryption | [7] |
| Compliance | SOC 2 Type II | [7] |

All variables (not just secrets) are encrypted with the workspace-specific
key [6].

## Secret Access Model

### Runtime Resolution

Secrets are never passed to callers directly. Instead [6]:

1. Variables are referenced as `$var:<variable_path>` strings in script
   parameters
2. At execution time, the worker resolves these references using the job's
   ephemeral token (`WM_TOKEN`)
3. The job inherits the caller's permissions — fails if insufficient access

### Client Library Access

Scripts can also fetch secrets programmatically [6]:
- Python: `wmill.get_variable("u/user/foo")`
- TypeScript: `wmill.getVariable('u/user/foo')`
- Bash: API calls using `WM_TOKEN` environment variable

### Permission Model

Variables follow an ownership path system [6]:
- `u/alice/secret` — only accessible by alice (unless shared)
- `f/devops/secret` — accessible by anyone with read access to that folder

## Credential Isolation from API Users

This directly addresses the requirement that the PA triggers workflows
without seeing credentials:

| Mechanism | How It Works | Source |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| Webhook triggers | Auto-generated for every script/flow; caller provides only the webhook URL and bearer token | [9] |
| Pre-scoped tokens | Limited to triggering a single script/flow; safe for sharing | [9] |
| Variable resolution | `$var:` references resolved by worker, never exposed to API caller | [6] |
| Ephemeral tokens | `WM_TOKEN` is job-scoped, inherits permissioned_as, not the caller's full permissions | [13] |

**Key property:** An API caller (the PA) triggers a workflow by webhook or
API call. The workflow uses credentials stored in Windmill. The PA never
sees the credential values — they're fetched by the worker at execution
time [6][9].

## Secret Masking

Job logs automatically mask secret values: first three characters visible,
remainder replaced with asterisks. This prevents accidental exposure even
when scripts log their inputs [6].

## Audit Logging

`variables.decrypt_secret` events are logged to the audit log whenever a
secret is accessed [6]. Audit logs are an Enterprise feature — Community
Edition shows redacted audit logs [23].

## External Secret Backends

| Backend | Authentication | Source |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| HashiCorp Vault | JWT, KV v2 engine | [6] |
| Azure Key Vault | Service principal (Get/Set/Delete) | [6] |

Both implement fail-closed design: if the external backend is unreachable,
operations fail rather than silently falling back to the database [6].

Bidirectional migration between database and external backends is
supported [6].

## Sensitive Input Handling

- Resources and script parameters can be marked as sensitive [6]
- Password fields render as masked inputs in the UI [6]
- `$jsonvar:` references store arbitrary JSON payloads as ephemeral secrets,
  fetched at execution time [6]

## Comparison to n8n

| Aspect | Windmill | n8n |
|--------|----------|-----|
| Encryption | Workspace-specific symmetric key | AES256 via N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY |
| Key management | Auto-generated per workspace | Auto-generated, must set for production |
| External backends | Vault, Azure Key Vault (built-in) | Vault, AWS Secrets Manager (Enterprise) |
| Audit logging | Yes (EE) | Not documented |
| Secret masking in logs | Yes (automatic) | Not documented |
| API credential isolation | Yes (by design) | Yes (credentials never in API responses) |

## Gaps and Limitations

- Specific encryption algorithm not documented (symmetric key described but
  AES vs ChaCha20 etc. unknown) [7]
- SECRET_SALT behavior and interaction with workspace key not fully
  explained [7]
- No published third-party cryptographic audit
- AWS KMS/Secrets Manager not listed as supported backend (only Vault and
  Azure Key Vault) [6]
